findings: codex plugin list --json does not expose skills, MCP servers, prompts or the interface displayName; only the version and policies. The skill names come from the app-server skills/list call inside the reproduction script.
codex mcp list shows the plugin server as agent-braid, without a plugin prefix.

The reproduction script restricts PATH to git, sh, uname and dirname, so the npm launcher codex.js fails (env: node: No such file or directory). The run passed with the native binary from the same npm package (@openai/codex-darwin-arm64) as --codex-executable. The script was not modified.

Two early observation mistakes were mine, not the plugin's: a hand-made AGENT_BRAID_HOME with mode 755 was refused by doctor (Owned plugin state must be private to its user), and a hand-made registry.json was refused (Unknown registry schema). State created by plugin setup passed.
